utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good morning. I apologise that because I had been sitting in another matter since 8.00, I am a little late this morning in here. Sir, could I remind you of the affirmation you made at the beginning of your evidence which still applies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Domazet.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in the courtroom. Good morning, Mr. Paunovic. We shall continue and I hope we shall conclude with my of the examination. Right at the outset, I have several questions for you about your evidence yesterday, about the meeting, the briefing on the 19th. You said how long it took and what you heard. Yesterday, you said that during that briefing, you didn't hear anything about the task involving the evacuation of the hospital; and since, based on what you said, that meeting took quite a long time do you remember at all what was discussed at this meeting or at the briefing, if you remember?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, I can't remember the details. I will repeat again that the evacuation of the hospital was discussed. As for some other details, I really can't remember now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did I understand you well that you said that it was discussed, or it wasn't discussed? I mean, the hospital.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you understood me well. The hospital evacuation that was to take place on the following day was discussed.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yesterday, you said that you attended almost all of the briefings or perhaps even all of the briefings. Do you remember the day before that, on the 18th, did you attend the briefing on that day and, if so, was the evacuation of the hospital discussed then?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the 18th of November, the evacuation of the hospital was not discussed. It couldn't have been discussed because, as I have told you, we came to the sector of the hospital on the 19th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I fully understand that, that you came on the 19th; however, why would that rule out the possibility of the evacuation of the hospital being discussed on the 18th in the evening; or is it your evidence that on the 18th, this was not discussed at all?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that the hospital was discussed at all on the 18th of November.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well, Mr. Paunovic. You spoke about the orders that you personally received from your commander, and in general. Can we agree that you said that you would normally receive those orders either in writing or verbally, somebody would transmit them to you, or via radio link; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Furthermore, as for the evacuation of the hospital, it is your evidence that you personally never saw a written order; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you know whether there was a written order about it or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. Perhaps there was one, but I have no information about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. If you personally didn't have occasion to see a written order, can you explain who conveyed what to you about your tasks in the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I said yesterday, my task was to secure the hospital, to search these persons, and to secure the buses. I didn't have any other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Who gave you this task?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As for the buses, the task was issued to me at the briefing on the 19th, that particular task. As concerns the search of the persons, as I explained yesterday, nobody specifically gave me that task because it falls under the regular procedure of the work of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this mean that right there on the spot, you realised that these people needed to be searched; and that without anybody's orders, you proceeded to search all of the persons leaving the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You said that it was your task to secure the buses. You explained yesterday how you did that. Tell me, please, as you did that in front of the hospital, did you -- as you were searching these people in front of the hospital, together with your policemen, were you aware of where these buses were supposed to go?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I knew was that these buses were supposed to go to the barracks in Vukovar. I think that I explained this in detail yesterday to Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this pertain to your explanation that they were supposed to go to the barracks in order to unite with those who were at the Velepromet and then go together to Sremska Mitrovica, was that the explanation you had in mind?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's the explanation that I had in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this mean that that particular moment, as you were in front of the hospital, you knew that the people boarding the buses were headed towards the JNA barracks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please take your statement, the one you gave to the military court -- or rather, your evidence before the military court. Let us see the part of your statement, and then I'm going to read it out and then I'll ask you to comment on it. This is page 3, somewhere towards the second half where a new paragraph begins, and it says there, I'm going to read slowly, and you'll tell me if you found it: "After that, I think it was on the 20th of November, 1991, everybody was evacuated from the hospital, but prior selection had been performed. The organ of security conducted a classification of people so some of them were separated aside to go to Croatia, some were earmarked to go to Vojvodina, and some were kept there and then put on buses which took them somewhere, but I don't know where." Let me continue with the quote and then we'll hear your comment: "The only thing I know is that my unit was tasked with securing a of civilians who were supposed to go to Croatia, and that the Croatian didn't want to let them in so they had to return. Then they were taken again, and I know they were turned over to Croats, but I don't know" Based on this, would you say that some six to seven years ago, your position was different from the one you gave us today? It says here that you didn't know where the people, who had been separated and put on buses, were headed.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't agree with you because what I said, what you just quoted, is correct. But when giving statements following this one, they put more detailed questions to me about these issues and conduct. You asked me about the group of buses that I gave you an explanation about yesterday. I said that they were headed to the barracks. But you have to realise that at the hospital, there were wounded, sick people; then there were civilians, and as I've said, members of the paramilitary formations of Croatia. So when I said, in my statement, that I didn't know where those buses went, I was referring to the buses which transported civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: And the civilians were put in those buses that were sent to Croatia and turned back; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how it was. I received this information several days after this event. I was not able to know this at the time, right away, that they would be sent back, that is, and that there would be problems in this respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. I agree you couldn't know this at that point in time, but I cannot agree with your explanation because it says quite clearly in your statement that one group was separated off to go to Croatia, another group to go to Vojvodina; and we agreed that these were all civilians and this is a third group. You say some were held back and taken into buses and took them off to somewhere but I don't know where. Will you agree with me that this third group can only refer to the ones who were separated off, searched by you, and who boarded the buses. It follows from your previous statement that you did not know then where those buses were going?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'll explain once again. You should realise what it was like at the hospital then. How can I remember where each bus was headed?

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. But seven years previously, this is how you remembered it and now you remember it differently. That's why I put this question to you. Please look at the last paragraph on this page, the third line from the bottom. You are probably responding a question by whoever was asking you the questions. You said: "Whether some people from the Vukovar Hospital were first taken to the barracks and then to the Ovcara farm, I don't know, because my unit had no tasks in this respect. All I know is that in Velepromet, in Vukovar, there were some kind of collection centre where all those who were considered to be prisoners were placed. Besides these, there were other people who were collected there as civilians; and from there, they were sent on to wherever they wanted to go." The first sentence in this passage shows that you were being asked about the barracks and Ovcara and this was your reply, you said you did not know anything about this because your unit had no tasks in this respect. So you repeated something that is in here and that I asked you about. My question is: Did you know that these buses were to go to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In this statement here, I'm saying that it was not my task to conduct persons to the Ovcara farm.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No. Mr. Paunovic, it says that you do not know whether they were taken first to the barracks and then to Ovcara. You said something quite different, that you didn't know whether they were taken either to the barracks or to Ovcara and that it was not your task. If we cannot agree on this, we will have to leave it up to others to decide. When you say that you knew they were going to the barracks, who told you this?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't remember that now.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. And yesterday, in response to my colleague, Mr. Bulatovic's question, you said they went to the barracks in order to be put together with the persons from Velepromet and then sent on to Mitrovica. Did you find this out -- in what way did you find this out?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already told you, I can't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. Yesterday, you said that those groups that were going towards the buses were searched in groups of about ten, that's what you said, that they stood next to the wall and then proceeded towards the buses; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: You also said there was a table on which property, I assume confiscated property, was to be placed; am I right?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Was anything else confiscated from those persons or was the search aimed solely at weapons and things that might pose a security risk?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When those persons were searched, apart from dangerous objects, as you say, nothing else was confiscated. Their personal belongings were left intact, except for those which could be used to inflict an injury on others. Their personal documents were not confiscated. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Although my question follows from your answer, the reply follows from what you just said, I'll still ask you this: Did your soldiers find money and jewelry, and were such things taken away from the people who were searched?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, right now I cannot remember whether, during the search, they found money. But if they did, it was certainly not confiscated because the soldiers were not doing this on their own initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Another question: Apart from your soldiers, that is, military policemen, were there any other soldiers or territorials participating in the search?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When performing this task, territorials, as you call them, and members of other units were not even present so they could not have conducted any searches. The search was carried out only by members of my battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. The persons who were searched and sent on towards the buses, were they able to walk unassisted, or did some of them need assistance, were some even on stretchers; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. The persons you are now referring to were all able to move, which means they walked to the buses unassisted.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. At any point in time before these buses left, did you approach the buses?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally did not approach the buses.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. If you did not approach the buses, would I be correct in concluding that you were not able to see whether there was a senior officer in each bus? I assume there was such an order and that there was an officer in each bus. I think you said something to that effect.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yesterday, I said that I didn't see all the buses, so of course I couldn't have seen all these officers. But one has to conclude that soldiers would not have been sent to perform such a task on their own.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, for counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does that mean that you consider due to the specific nature and importance of the task, it was important that on each bus, in addition to the two military policemen designated by you, there should also be an officer?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: As I understand it, you don't know whether these officers were actually there and who they were. Perhaps you do know.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know who they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I assume, then, that you cannot tell us whether they belonged to the military police or some other unit.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have just told you I can't remember who they were, in fact, I didn't even see them.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. As you say, that due to the nature of the task, in your view, it was necessary that an officer be on each bus, in addition to two military policemen providing security. My question is: If you knew, as you say, that they were going to the barracks, which is only a few kilometres away from the hospital, why was it so important in view of the distance, that they be escorted in this manner? Do you have any other explanation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, did you see Vukasinovic in front of the hospital at that time; do you recall?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I saw him in front of the hospital. He may have been near the buses, but I don't remember seeing him in front of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: I assume you saw the buses leaving. Did you stay at the hospital after that point; you didn't go to the barracks afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I personally was not in the hospital non-stop. I don't want it to be thought, on the basis of what I said yesterday and today, that this was the case. From time to time, I left to go to my command post which was located, at that point in time, behind the Vuteks playing field, sports field.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Go ahead, please, I didn't want to interrupt.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the hospital, the commander of the 4th Company was there all the time, Captain First Class Milivoje Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, wasn't the evacuation of the hospital such an important operation that you needed to be present all the time, or did you think it not necessary?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have been misunderstood. I didn't say I wasn't there during the evacuation. I said, rather, that I wasn't there all the time in the hospital area.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Very well. But you did spend most of your time that day in the hospital or in front of the hospital; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not the entire day, but yes. Yes, one could say that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Today, you said that you received no special orders from anyone about the search or your duties, but were you able to conclude who was in charge of the entire operation, which of the officers was in charge of evacuating the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said something about this yesterday. At the time of the evacuation, I saw Colonel Pavkovic there. Perhaps that was what I thought at the time. I had the impression that he was in charge of the operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Paunovic, my questions today about the departure the buses, and what I said about your not mentioning in your first statement about their going to the barracks or the Ovcara. First you said you didn't know, and today you say that you heard from someone that they were going to the barracks. Did you hear from anyone that they would go to Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, Ovcara was never mentioned at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did the military policemen, designated by you to escort the buses, go on to the Ovcara farm from the barracks; do you know that or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have this information.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: May I understand, then, that none of these military policemen or their officers ever briefed you about this or told you anything about it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this mean that, even today, you don't know whether your military policemen possibly went on from the barracks with those who were on the buses?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: The task you gave your military policemen that morning in the hospital, was it something that would be described as "escort duty" in your rules of service? You know what I'm referring to. That was one of the tasks of the military police.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One might say that with the proviso that the point to which persons were to be escorted was not something I told the soldiers. As you mentioned escort service, military policemen performed this task until they hand over the persons being escorted. Whether this happened in the barracks or somewhere else, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Do you consider that this manner of proceeding was in line with the rules of military service for the military police, in view of what you said yesterday and today?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, I spoke about the rules, but you must understand the special circumstances that obtained. Although I still consider that my soldiers performed their task well.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Mr. Paunovic, you spoke about that task, about them going to the buses and them going to the barracks; and then you said that somebody told you that they would all unite and then be sent to Sremska Mitrovica. What about your military policemen, the one that you assigned? Were they supposed to escort them further on all the way up to Sremska Mitrovica or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't know that. And the soldiers carried on with the task until it's completed. The soldiers cannot abandon buses halfway through and leave those people unattended.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Did you receive feedback from anyone, not only your military policemen, but from anyone as to what kind of tasks they performed from the moment you sent them off from the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Upon the completion of the task, commanders did not inform me about each individual patrol. I was informed that the mission was accomplished, that the soldiers had returned, or something along those lines. But I didn't receive individual information for each individual patrol.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Would you please tell me about the procedure of the hand-over of persons escorted by the military police?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand quite which hand-over do you have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Well, the location where the persons are taken to, the escorted persons, is there any document that is compiled on how that is done?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we are referring to the final destination, which is the prisoner's camp, during that final stage, a list is compiled; and then people are searched in detail and separated into various categories.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Thank you for this explanation. Can you tell us who does this? Who compiles these list? Who categorises people and so on?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The lists are made up in the prisoners' camp. It can be done by the commander or by a person designated by him or by somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: Does this pertain to the search and other acts as well?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As regards the camp, then, yes, other jobs are performed as well. A detailed search is conducted. If you need me to explain what a detailed search entails, I can do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: No. No, Mr. Paunovic. Just something briefly, is there a document on the hand-over that is signed? Did they receive a document that the hand-over was completed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were supposed to receive only a document confirming the number of people handed over.

utterances.speaker: MR. DOMAZET
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Paunovic. I don't have any further questions for you. Your Honours, I have completed my cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Domazet. Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Good morning, Mr. Paunovic. Yesterday, you said that the first platoon of your 3rd Company was attached to the 1st Motorised Battalion commanded by Borivoje Tesic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind and tell us what tasks they performed within the 1st Motorised Battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't be able to answer that question. I don't know what tasks they performed.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did they secure the command post of Borivoje Tesic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A part of the unit, I don't know whether, perhaps, it was the entire unit secured the command post of the 1st Motorised Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you, at any point in time, go to the command post of the 1st Motorised Battalion to tour, to visit your men, members of your unit? And did you see them there securing that command post?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On several occasions, I went to the command post of the 1st Motorised Battalion. When I went to the command post, I saw my soldiers. Naturally, I wouldn't see all of them. The ones I saw worked on reception tasks and performed guard duty at the command post.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, do you know whether anybody could come to that command post, any soldier, or did your military policemen, those performing reception duty and guard duty, control ingress and egress, and did they supervise that? And could you please speak a little bit faster? There is no need to speak a little bit slow, if we all fall asleep in the courtroom there will be nobody listening to you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear that not everybody had access to the command post. The commander of the platoon received an order from the commander, to whom he was subordinated, as to who was entitled to enter. And one can, based on that, conclude that people didn't have open access to the command post, whenever they wanted and whoever wanted.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. When arrested by the members of your unit, when somebody is arrested by the members of your unit, if force is used on that occasion, is there a requirement to compile some kind of a written report about that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the method used. When a rubber baton is used, then there is a requirement to write a written report.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you ever hear and were you ever informed that members of your unit, who were attached to the 1st Motorised Battalion beat the volunteers, or some other members, who were attached to companies when they were arrested? Did you ever hear something like that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. You said yesterday that on the 19th of November, 1991, you sent Captain Simic to secure the hospital. My question is: How long after him did you, yourself, go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could be said that Simic and I arrived almost simultaneously to the hospital sector.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Who arrived first?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that now. I think that it was me, but he arrived shortly thereafter. The time difference was minor.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday, you also said how you replaced Tesic's men, that they secured the hospital. And that when you arrived, they withdrew and that you created a proper security force. In the police sense, you created a reception desk, then you created patrols, and so on; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Would you please tell us, where did you establish the reception desk?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first one was at the entrance into the hospital compound, and then there were various reception posts at the areas where one could leave the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 19th or the 20th, could any soldiers or officers enter the hospital to check the patients, mistreat people and so on, or was it the case that nobody could either come in or come out?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody could either come in or come out. That was my task and I accomplished my task.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: During the night, on the 19th of November, did somebody come in and mistreat the wounded in the hospital or not?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Where did you find the equipment and the weapons? The evidence that you gave yesterday, in which part of the hospital did you find those items?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The majority of the equipment was found around the hospital. There was some containers around the hospital, then there were large mounds of sand. The weapons were dug in the sand and then they were also in containers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Do you know where the entrance into emergency room was at the time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: In relation to that emergency room entrance, and in relation to Gunduliciva Street, where were those containers located. Was it close to Gunduliciva Street?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were some there near Gunduliceva, but in relation to the emergency room also on the other side of the hospital, and there was a large pile of sand there, as far as I can remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: So does this mean on both sides?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 19th of November in the course of the day or not, did you see Captain Radic in any location either within the hospital compound or within the hospital itself?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. On the 20th of November, you said that you ordered that the people from the hospital be searched. My question is: Who ordered that these people be taken from the hospital to the buses where Vukasinovic stood?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Was your question who ordered?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: That was my first question.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't remember that now. I know who was in command. I know that this was done by my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Did Captain Radic take any part in triage, in the search, or in taking away of the people to the buses which were in front of the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Captain Radic didn't do that, and as I said, he wasn't present there either on the 19th or on the 20th in the sector of the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Could any commander of any company issue an order to the military policemen or not, unless that commander is commander of the military police company?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only in one case. If that entire unit is attached to his unit, and then based on an order, he is in command. That is the only case, the only scenario.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. Did you hear, and did you see - because we here in the courtroom heard from a witness - that 15 to 20 people who were on the list, once they left from the hospital to the barracks, were returned from the barracks to the hospital. Did you hear about that, 15 to 20 people from the barracks were returned to the hospital as family members of hospital staff?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Perhaps there were such cases but I can't remember that. I really can't.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. My last question: Do you know who did you give your statement to, the statement that you gave to the Hague investigators?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean which person?

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: Yes?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The gentleman from the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: What's his name? Is it Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the person to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: All right. This is the OTP expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no further questions, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Borovic. Mr. Weiner, is it most practical for you to proceed now or after an early break?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It doesn't make a difference. If the Court would like a break now, that's fine with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It's a matter of what will suit you most, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We could take a break now. A cup of coffee or tea is always pleasant before cross.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If you're lucky you might have time for that, yes. We will resume at 25 minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] A technical question, Your Honours. I have spoken to Mr. Weiner, and he informed me that he will take a session and a half, a little less than two sessions. So if there is redirect, if there is a little time left, could the next witness not be called, or shall we wait until we see what happens after the next session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: If we finish this witness today, I think we need not move to the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Any other adventurous ideas? Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Paunovic, my name is Phil Weiner. I'm with the Office of the Prosecutor, and I'm going to be asking you some questions this morning. Now, you were familiar with the 80th Motorised Brigade, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say that I was familiar with it, but I know what brigade this is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, that it was largely made up of reservists; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you testified that it had a police company in it, didn't you? A military police company.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And was that also largely comprised of reservists?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, the Guards Motorised Brigade had military police units, and those were not largely comprised of reservists; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now -- excuse me, sir. I would like to refer you to the statement you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. It's 04238944 to 04238966 in the e-court. And I'd like to go to page 13, paragraph 66, which is 04238956, 8956, Madam Registrar. That will come up in front of you very shortly. There's an English and a B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have a B/C/S version if the defendants would like to follow along on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I think that could be a good idea, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I invite your attention to the next to last sentence in paragraph 56 -- I'm sorry, paragraph 66. Do you see that where it says,"I agree that it was not logical." Do you see that, first? Do you see that sentence, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. I don't know what sentence you're referring to. Is it in paragraph 66?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Paragraph 66, the next to last sentence, it begins with the words: "I agree that it was not logical." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'll read it to you, sir: "I agree that it was not logical to delegate the responsibility for the protection of the evacuees to the military police company of the 80 Motorised Brigade, knowing that the Guards Motorised Brigade," or you use GM, TB, R, "has two battalions of military police to accomplish this task." Is that what it says there, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's your signature at the bottom of the page?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And sir, could you please explain why it was not logical to delegate the responsibility of protecting the evacuees to the military police company of the 80th, where you stated that the Guards Motorised Brigade had two battalions of military police. Could you please explain that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time I was making this statement, I did not know that they had been entrusted to this company of the military police. So when the investigator convinced me that they had been handed over to that company of the military police, that was my opinion at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, please explain why it wasn't logical to hand over the evacuees to the military police company of the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying to explain to you, but I can't do it in a single sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, isn't it true that you always assumed that the evacuees had been handed over to the military police of the 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, could you look at the first full sentence on that same page, right at the top. I'll read it in English, please follow along: "I always assumed that the evacuees had been handed over to the military police of the 80th Motorised Brigade." Isn't that what it says, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says. But I'm telling you when the investigator put something to me, this was the statement I made. I don't remember exactly what happened then.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Why would it be illogical to hand those evacuees over to the 80th Motorised Brigade?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that point in time, what I stated was guided by the fact that there were two military police battalions in the Guards Brigade; and without entering into the problem any deeper, that is, without taking into consideration that they were already busy with other tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also knew, sir, that the Guards Motorised Brigade units, or military police units, were better trained than the military police units in the 80th Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. One could say that, although I didn't know how well-trained this company of the military police was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you also knew that your unit had two military police -- I'm sorry, that there were two military police battalions in the Guards Motorised Unit with hundreds of members of military police; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you knew that there were two military police companies in the Guards Motorised Brigade that were equipped with armoured personnel carriers; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Just a correction, Your Honour, on page 24, line 15, there were two military police battalions in the Guards Motorised Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Was it two guards motorised battalions or companies with armoured personnel carriers?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're mixing battalions and companies up here, but I'll explain. The Guards Brigade, in its establishment, had two military police battalions. In the establishment of the 1st Battalion of the military police, there were two companies and two APCs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And also, the Guards Motorised Brigade had the only anti-terrorist unit in the SFRY armed forces; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It had an anti-terrorist company.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Not just an anti-terrorist company, the only one in the SFRY armed forces.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, that was probably the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So, sir, if there was an order or a task was issued on November 20th, the Guards Motorised Brigade military police battalions had the resources available to protect the prisoners or evacuees; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. This was the area of responsibility of the 80th Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, if an order or task was issued on November 20th, the Guards Motorised military police battalions had the resources available to protect those prisoners; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the Guards Motorised Brigade military police battalions could have sent its members to Ovcara to protect the prisoners if the commander issued that order.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was the battalion commander not the brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If Colonel Mrksic, the brigade commander and commander of operational Group South, issued and an order to the Guards Motorised Brigade military police battalions to go to Ovcara to protect those prisoners, they could have done it.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly they would have carried out the commander's order.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if that commander ordered those military police battalions to provide around-the-clock security for those prisoners at Ovcara, that could have been done.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I assume so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know, sir, that no such orders or tasks were ever issued on November 20th, 1991; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And would you agree that Colonel Mrksic was your commander, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you agree that Colonel Mrksic was your commander?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did say that. He was my brigade commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the commander's advisor or Colonel Mrksic's advisor on the use of the military police was Major Sljivancanin, as the security organ; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as the advisor, he could have counselled Colonel Mrksic on the use of the military police.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he could have.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as advisor, it was his job to discuss threat assessments with Colonel Mrksic.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I assume that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And he could have advised Colonel Mrksic as to the use of the police based on threat assessments; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Depends on what he -- what assessment he made. If that was the assessment he made, then that's probably the advice he gave.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: If an assessment was made that a threat or serious threat occurred, then advice could be given on the use of military police; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. We'll get back to the prisoners a little bit later, but I have some more just general questions for you. You mentioned that you had two military police battalions; and within one of the battalions was a crime scene, an investigation section; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the 1st Battalion, according to the establishment, there was a crime prevention squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And within that crime prevention squad was a crime scene investigation section.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the establishment of my battalion, this was not there. So how they were organised precisely, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In the 1st Military Police Battalion, there was a crime scene investigation unit; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. It had a different name. It was called the crime prevention squad.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when -- within that crime prevention squad was crime scene investigation and other aspects of criminal investigation for crimes; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that within this squad, there was some other section or squad. This was not part of the establishment of the 2nd Battalion of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, let's continue on your statement to the ICTY which was a little over a year ago, given a little over a year ago. Could we go to page 3, paragraph 17. And page 3, for the record, is 04238946. Sir, do you have it in front of you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I'll read it. "The 1st MP," or military police battalion,"was organised as follows: The commander with his command (i.e., staff) a section for crime fighting, (crime scene investigation and other aspects of criminal investigation for crimes that fell within the jurisdiction of the military courts)." Does that refresh your recollection, sir, that there was a crime scene investigation and other aspects of criminal investigation personnel within that 1st military police battalion?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid we don't understand each other. I'm not trying to evade this. What I said is correct. It says "crime prevention squad" here. And in parenthesis, it refers to this squad, not some other squad, which would be part of this squad. It deals with pre-investigative activities. They deal with pre-criminal proceedings for crimes falling within the competence of military courts. So this is the squad in question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. While in Vukovar, were you or anybody else in the military police, asked to investigate any crimes or murders occurring in Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Neither I nor the members of my unit were asked to do this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In 1991 and 1992 in Belgrade, were you ever asked to investigate any murders or crimes which occurred in Ovcara?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, you're not aware of any investigation in 1991 and 1992 relating to the murders or other crimes that occurred in Ovcara; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not aware of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You've testified that an evacuation operation is a complex process; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it requires the consideration of various military matters ranging from road plan, to hand-over, to protection of evacuees. It requires a number of factors for consideration; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And usually there is a written order defining the tasks and discussing all of these factors; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And within that order is a risk or threat assessment; isn't that required as part of an evacuation process?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I said that in my statement to the best of my recollection, referring to what should have been in that order, including that assessment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if there is a threat to the evacuees, it must be neutralised or dealt with.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Regardless of whether there is or is not a threat, it always has to be assumed or, rather, one always has to decide what has to be done should such a threat arise.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's part of the planning and anticipation which is necessary in an evacuation; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. We can say that this is planning and anticipation before the task was carried out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that you can't ignore any threats.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, I would like to show you a document which you discussed with the OTP investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown Exhibit 581, please. It's called, "The Participation of Military Police in Guarding Prisoners of War."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you familiar with that document, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you discussed that document with the investigators, or you at least mentioned that you were familiar with that document to them.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And would you agree that even though that manual, that training manual that you have in front of you is dated 1993, the methods for guarding prisoners as described in that manual also applied in 1991.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can partially agree. I don't remember exactly what it looked like in 1991, but something resembling this, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you said in paragraph 44 of your statement that this manual was also valid for 1991, you still agree with that statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I gave such a statement. It sounds a bit illogical what I said, but I agree that there is no major difference between the initial manual and this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And I just want to refer you to one page, page 28 of that manual. Page 28 in the English. And just the first part of it,. "Security is aimed at preventing prisoners of war from attempting to escape and rejoin in their armed forces, liberation attempts by members of their armed forces and supporters on the ground, and attempts to kill or torture them." One of the reasons for security is to protect the prisoners from being attacked, tortured, or murdered; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what it says in that rule, too.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if you go to page 29, the last paragraph, it says -- 29 with the text. I think it's 28 that's being shown. 29 in the English. "In order to protect prisoners of war from reprisals carried out by local population during transfer through inhabited areas that they have terrorised, security can be augmented with a cordon which requires stronger security forces." Are you familiar with that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I am familiar with that. Everything you're saying is contained in that rule.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know from that that when you bring prisoners through an area where local people are hostile towards them, you must anticipate the chance that a problem can occur or attempts will be made to attack them, hurt them, injure them, or kill them.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When carrying out an attack of that nature - now that you're quoting it - there is a previous paragraph where it says that an attempt should be made not to go through such areas, but if it's necessary, then additional measures are to be taken in order to avoid precisely the cases that you enumerate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd like to turn to another section in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. Paragraph 72 to 77, page 14 which is 04238957. While we're waiting for that to come up, let me ask you some questions about that. While you served in Vukovar from September 30th to November 24th, there were no civilian police forces in existence.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I could see at the time, no, they were not in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Because if they existed, you would have had to have some contact with them as fellow police officers; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you never had any such contact?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And while you were in Vukovar, you were not aware of any functioning judicial bodies.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you never dealt with any civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And there was never any discussion at any of those briefings or meetings at the OG South command concerning civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And there were never any orders issued at those OG South command meetings in relation to your dealing with civilian authorities; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, if there was a crime that occurred such as civilian looting, the security organ and the crime prevention section of the 1st Military Police Battalion would do the investigation and make the arrests, because there were no functioning police, civilian police, or judicial bodies.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, your police battalion had a war diary.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that was maintained while you were in Vukovar.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you listed all orders that you received in that war diary.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you listed them not only that you received them and what they were, but who issued those orders; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. You know yourself what a war diary looks like.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes. And they are listed by date, not only the orders received, the activities which you executed are listed by date.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have this war diary with you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When did you last review the war diary?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The last time I looked at it was in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever make a request for it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm assuming it's in Belgrade in the military archives.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know where it is now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you don't even know whether it exists; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say either way that it exists or it doesn't. All war diaries are normally kept at the brigade command. During the war operations, a unit, a battalion, keeps a war diary. But once the combat operations are completed, the diary is turned over and it is kept in a secure way at the brigade command. This applies to all diaries, not just to my diary.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, did you maintain a personal diary or personal calendar describing your activities by date?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I had no personal diary or personal calendar. Every commander from the lowest level to the highest level typically had a notebook where some basic tasks were recorded.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you maintain this notebook while in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you have that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. The same applies to these notebooks, they are considered official documents. When one is issued with a notebook, that notebook is recorded in the registration books at the command. Once it is completed, or perhaps the person whose notebook it is, is transferred to another unit, such a notebook is returned, which is what I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And within this notebook and the diary, would all oral orders be listed?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can't say that all of them would be listed, some were brief; and perhaps I didn't record them in the notebook. As for longer orders, yes, I certainly recorded them. But now after so many years, I really can't remember all of the details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And orders such as those relating to an evacuation would be listed in the diary or notebook.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And having not looked at either of these documents since 1991, you're testifying today solely on the basis of your memory.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One couldn't say so. In the introductory part, I said to whom I gave statements. In this statement as well, there were many paragraphs where the investigator put some documents to me. And that refreshed my memory and I was able to link the documents with some events. So what I'm telling you today is not simply a reflection of what I remember from 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But since there were no documents relating to the evacuation, that portion of your testimony is solely related to your memory.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct; however, I don't know whether there are documents concerning the evacuation of the hospital or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that in a bit. Now, you testified that you had attended briefings or meetings at the command of the Operation Group South in Negoslavci.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you're familiar with the members of that Operations Group South command, the command staff.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that the Operations Group South consisted of the Guards Motorised Brigade, and some attached units.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you knew that in October of 1991, Colonel Mrksic was named the commander of the -- I'm sorry, Colonel Mrksic of the Guards Motorised Brigade was named the commander of Operations Group South.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We knew that he was the commander but he didn't come in and say to us, "I am the commander of the Operations Group South from today on." We saw that in the orders. After all, he was our brigade commander, nothing bad about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you know that the Guards Brigade commander, Colonel Mrksic, and the command staff and that of Operations Group South were one and the same.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are probably referring to something similar that I stated either in the statement or before the special court, and my conclusion was based on the following: When we attended briefings, brigade commander Colonel Mrksic was still my superior, that is to say, at the brigade command. I didn't see any other officers from other formations who had been sent to be additional staff on this command, at least that was my conclusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you knew or you concluded that the command staff and the commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade and OG South were one and the same.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was my conclusion, which doesn't necessarily mean that it was a correct one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, it was more than your conclusion. You stated that you knew that, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I already said to you that I mentioned something of that nature in some previous statements, and I'm now not denying it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So when you stated to the Office of the Prosecutor, in paragraph 23 on page 5: "I know that the command staff and commander of the Guards Motorised Brigade and Operations Group South were one and the same," you're not denying that, are you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can deny it only partially. I can deny only some words. Yes, that's true I stated that, but there's a big difference between saying "I know" or "I think"; however, what I stated here is correct and I don't see any contentious about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yesterday, you mentioned that there was a triage or selection process in the hospital; do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And do you agree that that selection process was carried out by the security organs?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organs were present, yes, but there were other elements there, doctors, some others I can't remember. It wasn't just them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you agree, sir, that the selection process was carried out exclusively by the security organs under the direction of Major Sljivancanin?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I wouldn't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You just mentioned doctors. You testified yesterday that there were doctors involved in this selection. Were these JNA doctors, Yugoslav People's Army doctors?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the time, I didn't know the doctors. Whether they were the JNA doctors or civilians or both of them, I wouldn't be able to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that it was the local doctors at the hospital who assisted in the selection process?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There were doctors from elsewhere. They were not from the Guards Brigade, perhaps they were from the 1st Military District. I don't know. I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that no such thing happened, that doctors were not involved in the selection process, and that you know that; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your position. My position is quite different, that the doctors, together with security organs and other people, participated in the triage or selection, as you call it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, we've talked about the statement that you gave to the Office of the Prosecutor. When you gave the statement, did you tell the truth?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told the truth then and I'm doing the same now. It all depends on how the questions were phrased by the investigator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And after you gave the statement, you signed each and every page; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, but it was an English version. I didn't sign a Serbian one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And after you gave your statement, sir, it was read back to you in the Serbian language, and you signed that it was read back to you; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you are correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you signed that it was true, to the best of your knowledge and recollection; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I can't remember those details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May be witness be shown page 04238960 which is page 17.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see that in front of you, sir? Do you see where it says, "Witness acknowledgment"?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And it first sentence says, "This statement has been read over to me in the Serbian language and is true to the best of my knowledge and recollection." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you signed below that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown paragraph 60 beginning on pages 11 and going into page 12. It's page 12 in the signed version which is 04238955. ERN 04238955.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you have that in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 60, you mean?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, sir. I'll read it, why don't you follow along. "The selection was aimed at identifying members of the Croatian forces who were hiding in the hospital. The security organs had information that among the people in the hospital, there were indeed members of the Croatian forces. I do not know how the security organs were carrying out the selection -- or who were carrying out the selection were able to determine who belonged to the Croatian forces and who did not." "I do not know whether any medical personnel from the JNA were involved in the selection process. As far as I know, only the medical staff of the hospital was there. I do not know, either, whether anyone from the ICRC or International Community participated in the selection. I did not see anyone from the TO present during the selection process, but then I did not know anyone from the TO." "So in conclusion, I believe that the selection was carried out exclusively by members of the security organs of OG South under the direction of Major Veselin Sljivancanin, chief of the security organs of the Guards Motorised Brigade." Did I read that out correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And will you agree that you signed the bottom of that particular page?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you seem to be concentrating on the signature. I can say that I signed in English. What I said is correct. However, this refers to the selection of personnel, not triage. The security organ cannot carry out a triage in order to establish whether someone is injured or ill. I am not trying to evade what I said, that the security organs participated in selecting people, because I assume they had information as to who was in the hospital.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said that, "This selection was carried out exclusively by members of the security organs." You never mention any doctors participating here; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mention doctors. I didn't say they were from the JNA. Maybe they were not part of the JNA. I was not saying specifically that they were from the JNA because I didn't know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you say anywhere in this paragraph that the selection unit or the key persons who performed the selection and those who performed the triage were different?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you say anywhere in this paragraph that the persons who performed the triage and those who performed the selection were different?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. The investigator probably didn't ask me that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you say anywhere in this paragraph or anywhere in this statement or in any other statement or testimony that you've ever given other than yesterday or today that doctors were involved in a triage or selection?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have said that, but I can't recall now whether I did or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Proofing notes were filed upon the Office of the Prosecutor on November 1st and November 2nd. Do you accept that no mention was made in either of those proofing notes that doctors were involved in a triage at the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Did you ever tell counsel that doctors were involved in a triage or selection process at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall telling them that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you just thought about it for the first time yesterday when you testified for the first time in 15 years.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that I said it for the first time yesterday, because I cannot remember all the details of each and every one of my statements. In this case, I did not discuss this in detail with the lawyers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the first time you ever recall discussing it in detail was yesterday, 15 years after the incident.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct. I may have spoken about it before. That's what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please tell us, when did you speak of this in your statement at the -- to the Belgrade military court, to the special court in Belgrade. We know you didn't mention it in your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor. When did you ever discuss this previously or mention it previously?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said I couldn't remember when I mentioned it. It's different when you are talking and linking certain events to others, your memory gets refreshed, things jog your memory. And everything I said, not just in this paragraph or in this statement, is 100 percent correct. There may be things to add, but probably it was because that's how questions were put to me by the investigators.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you mentioned it yesterday suddenly because a question was put to you.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. You said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, when you accept that you have never mentioned this statement previously, at the break you can examine your testimony before the Belgrade court or the Belgrade military court, you can look at your prior testimony, you've never mentioned it previously. And having never mentioned it previously and not believing you discussed this matter with the attorneys, the Defence attorneys who have called you, what is the basis for you suddenly saying yesterday that doctors were involved in the triage or selection process?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember what the question was yesterday, but I do remember talking about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And would you agree, sir, if you accept you've never mentioned it in any of your prior statements, that was the first time in 15 years that you've ever mentioned that to anyone?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat again: I can't recall everything. I don't accept this. If I didn't say something before and you now ask me about it, it doesn't mean that I omitted it purposely before.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you agree you've never mentioned it previously in 15 years?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. Yesterday, you also testified about groups of civilians being outside the hospital. You testified to that at pages 22 and 23. Do you recall that testimony?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean in the statement to the investigator or yesterday? I didn't understand you correctly, sorry. Could you please repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yesterday in your testimony, you testified about groups of armed civilians cursing, issuing provocations, being outside the hospital; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do. Now I understand your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you testified that you didn't consider these groups to be a threat, yesterday; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And in fact, you also testified in Belgrade at the special court that you didn't believe these groups to be a threat; do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If that's what it says in the statement, probably I did. But as for the details, I can't remember everything I said in detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
