utterances.text: Are you aware that a member of the press has testified in this case, at page 3118, that he also arrived in Vukovar on November 19th and saw soldiers drinking heavily and firing weapons? Did you see anything like that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know what you're talking about. I don't know what journalist, what soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: A journalist testified that in the city centre of Vukovar - and we're not speaking of New York City or Tokyo; we're speaking about Vukovar, in the city centre - there were soldiers who were drinking heavily and firing off weapons. Did you also see that while you were in Vukovar centre and at the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sir, if you're not talking about New York, I'm not talking about Belgrade. This journalist may have seen that with his own eyes, but I did not see it with mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The journalist also indicated that there were people who were calling themselves Chetniks walking around, and that they were setting up musical systems to play music throughout the area. Did you see these people who were drinking heavily too?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that members of the international press on that day feared that a massacre would happen, and they made a plan to split up and cover as much of the area as they could to prevent a massacre from occurring? Were you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid this is a very complicated question. Could you please repeat it and give me a precise date? And could you put it briefly? This question seems to contain more than one question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Were you aware that on November 19th, members of the international press in Vukovar centre feared that a massacre would happen? They made a plan to split up so they could cover as much area as they could to prevent a massacre from occurring. Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm afraid I have to repeat again, I didn't hear that and who was supposed to split up, the journalists? And where did the journalists get this information?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The journalists got the information from seeing the drunken Chetniks and soldiers walking around firing guns, which you didn't see any of that, did you, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm telling you the journalists could have seen all sorts of things, but I did not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Isn't it true, sir, that you increased the security due to this threat?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What security are you referring to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said that you increased the security at the hospital. Wasn't it due to this threat; these drunken soldiers walking around through the streets, and the chance that some harm would come to the people in the hospital; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not correct. Had there been such a threat, I would have either strengthened the security on my own initiative and then informed the brigade commander about it, or had the brigade commander had such information, he personally would have ordered me to strengthen the security with a company or more, whereas the strengthening that you are referring to amounted to only one platoon which arrived only on the following day. Yesterday, I described what its task was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Whose decision was it to increase the security, yours or the brigade commander's?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At my proposal, the commander issued this order to me. Every movement of every unit was something that I had to inform my superior officer about. He had to know where my units were.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you testified yesterday as to your reasons for increasing the security, and those related to the evacuation and the escorting of vehicles. Wasn't that your testimony at page 24 yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you testified yesterday, you said, "I had one company securing the hospital, but the company was not at its full complement and I knew that I would be needing personnel to provide escort to vehicles carrying evacuees. Furthermore, I needed men to frisk people upon leaving the hospital and to avoid undermining the overall security system. I ordered for this platoon to be involved." Do you recall that testimony yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, 15 months ago, you testified before the Belgrade special court, and you were asked about the increase in security and you gave conflicting answers; do you recall that? Answers that conflict with the testimony you gave yesterday. You don't recall?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall every detail of everything. You always adhere to everything I said, but if I were to give a statement next month, it would not be exactly the same, not because I would be lying, but simply because one cannot recall everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Your Honour, can we move to his Belgrade testimony now, or would you like to take the lunch break or the 20-minute break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I would be thinking of about another ten minutes or so, Mr. Weiner, is that a practical time?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. May the witness be shown e-court Belgrade testimony 0461-9343 through 0461-9395. Page 9 in the English version of the Belgrade testimony which would be 0461-9348. Page 9 in the English version. In the B/C/S, page 9348. And if you could move down on the page to where the presiding judge says, "I understand. Was there any reason to increase security?" It should be towards the middle of the page.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the judge says, "I understand. Was there any reason to increase security? I mean was there an objective reason, an objective need in that sense?" Witness Radoje Paunovic: "I don't know. The command's assessment that it should be. I don't know. To tell you the truth, I didn't discuss this as far as I recall. This was a regular order and I had the men." Presiding judge: "I understand. But you were a commander and you were asked to reinforce security, and so I'm asking you if you have any information or recollections in that respect as to the reason for this, what were the assessments about?" "To tell you the truth, I cannot. It's been 13 years. I can remember some details, but that ..." And then they ask you if there were any problems, and you say no. When did you first realise -- first, is that your testimony; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this statement, yes. I mean, yes, about the statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In the proofing notes and the witness summary provided by the Defence during the summer and last week, there is no mention of the reasons that you testified to yesterday for increasing the security. Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about anybody's testimony. I'm not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: We're talking about the summary of your testimony. The Defence has never notified the Prosecution, the Court, or Defence counsel that were going to change or provide new statements as to the reason for the additional security. Are you aware of that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not in my sphere of competence. I don't understand you. Why have I come here then? You could have read all the statements and come to your conclusions; both you and the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: One and a half years ago, you were asked by the Court, and you were told -- and you stated that you didn't know why the commander chose to increase security. Yesterday, you testified it was your decision to increase security, and you provided all of these reasons for it. In the past year and a half, when did you arrive at these reasons for increasing security and realise that it was your decision to increase security?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall every detail now. It was mostly the court investigator who refreshed my memory because he showed me many documents. If I signed something, not just this statement, but in general, it doesn't mean I remember every detail. Of course I signed this statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor, you never provided the information which you testified yesterday as to the reason for increasing security; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say I stated that before the court investigator. But in my testimony before him, which lasted for two days, many documents were shown to me, and perhaps these documents contributed to jogging my memory with respect to certain issues. And even now, I cannot remember every detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, in no statement that you have ever given previously or your testimony at the Belgrade special court, did you ever mention those reasons, which you testified to yesterday, and that it was your decision to increase security. So when, in the past 15 years, did you suddenly realise the information that you provided yesterday?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: 15 years ago, and yesterday I recalled it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you never mentioned this in your proofing to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody asked me. If they had, I might have. But nobody asked me about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So yesterday, for the first time in 15 years, you recalled it?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recall it. Yesterday was the first time I was asked about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, you were asked directly by the presiding judge in Belgrade, and you couldn't answer a year and a half ago; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question wasn't put like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you told the Belgrade presiding judge that you didn't know the reasons for increasing security, were you telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I always tell the truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you didn't --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But it could also be that on that occasion, I simply could not recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you suddenly recalled yesterday for the first time?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't recall. I'm telling you for the hundredth time that yesterday, they put a question to me and I answered that question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, is it time to take the break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner. We will resume at 25 minutes to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Good afternoon. Good afternoon, sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, isn't it true that you received tasks and orders from Major Sljivancanin while in Vukovar?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that it wasn't possible for Major Sljivancanin to issue you orders or tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown his statement, his 1998 statement to the military court in Belgrade, 0218-8231 to 0218-8234 at page 2, which is 0218-8232 in the English; and it's also page 2 in the B/C/S, 8232. Could you go down to where the narrative is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Can we go to, sir, the middle. Do you see the words "That is when I got an order"? It's after the words -- do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Okay. And you stated to the military court: "That is when I got an order, as far as I can remember, from the brigade staff chief, Lieutenant Colonel Miodrag Panic, or maybe from Major Veselin Sljivancanin, chief of brigade security, to go along with the part of the unit that was at Mitnica, to go towards the hospital and to take over security of the hospital in Vukovar." Did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You read it out correctly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And of all your statements, sir, this statement here, this 1999 statement was closest in time to that particular order.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct, but not in 1998, rather 1999, although it's not much of a difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And, sir, you signed -- this statement is in Serbian, or Bosnian/Croatian/Serbian, and you signed it. It's in your native tongue and you signed it, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And above your signature, on page 4 in the English and also page 4 in the B/C/S, which is 8234, you wrote -- or it's written: "I will not read the record because I was listening to dictation, and everything is into record as I stated it and I will sign it without complaint." And then you signed that. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's beyond dispute.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So do you agree in 1999, you conceded that Major Sljivancanin could have issued orders to you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you read out in the first part of this statement, I said that I received that order from the Chief of Staff, and it's true that I said "maybe". I added "maybe"; it was given by Major Sljivancanin. I wasn't that it was him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So the fact that you said it could have been given by Major Sljivancanin, you are conceding that Major Sljivancanin could have issued orders to you; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's not logical. I said about who had issued the order. This involves just this one occasion. I said "maybe".

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So by saying maybe it came from Major Sljivancanin, sir, you're admitting that this initial order may have come from Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I disagree with that. You're just building assumptions on that basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you stated that the order may have come from Major Sljivancanin; isn't that correct? That's what you stated.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says here "maybe" but I'm telling you how it was in reality.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're telling us or you're testifying today that it came from Panic. But in 1999, you told the military court that it came from either Panic or maybe from Major Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why aren't you quoting first what I said, that I received it from Panic. Why are you just focussing on Sljivancanin? I said from the Chief of Staff, Panic, and then it's true that I said "maybe from Sljivancanin." At any rate, you can ask Panic if he comes here to testify. Perhaps he remembers that better; perhaps he doesn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So by saying you may have received it from Major Sljivancanin, you are admitting that you could have received orders from Major Sljivancanin; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't accept that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You said -- since Mr. Panic is coming here, maybe we should ask Mr. Panic. Are you aware that Mr. Panic has given a statement, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose that he gave statement, maybe not about this particular detail. But I'm sure that he must have given some statements. He was Chief of Staff, after all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And are you aware that Mr. Panic or Colonel Panic gave a statement to that same military court as you did?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know where he gave his statements. I think I know about the military court but I don't know about other occasions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And were you aware, sir, that Major Panic has denied ever giving you an order to go to the hospital and cordoning it off?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again as a matter of principle just as the last time, I think that finally the time has come for us to put an end to this and to limit this putting of statements to witnesses. We had a case where Mr. Domazet was putting to the witness what the witness said. What can be said to the witness is that a certain person said this and that, and then we can give the details about that particular witness, the name and so on. After all, Mr. Panic will be coming here to the courtroom. I think that what is happening here is that the OTP is trying to challenge what this witness is saying in an indirect way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: There is a difference on this occasion; it was the witness which introduced the prospect that it was Mr. Panic. So I think we'll leave counsel to get on with his cross-examination. Thank you. Mr. Weiner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, the question is: Were you aware that Major Panic has denied ever giving you an order to go to the hospital and cordoning it off?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about such a statement, nor was his statement put to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Based on your lack of records, sir, or diary, and based on Colonel Panic's statement that he didn't issue an order, will you concede that someone other than Colonel Panic ordered you and your unit to the Vukovar Hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we read this text again, by your leave, I'm going to repeat my words, "I received orders at the time," and this bit is important, "as far as I can remember now, I did sign this statement." But I put in here "as far as I remember, I didn't receive anything from Sljivancanin or Panic." I cannot claim with certainty, but I definitely did not receive it from Sljivancanin. As for what Panic stated, I don't know. Perhaps his memory is faulty; perhaps mine is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, since your memory might be faulty, will you concede that someone other than Colonel Panic ordered you to go to the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Who would that other person be?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, as noted in your --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you wish me to say that it was Sljivancanin who ordered it? You keep insisting on it, so you would be happy if I said that and we would proceed, right? I can't remember, and I stand by my statement. I signed it, but I can't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, in 1999, you notified the Court, the military court in Belgrade, that Major Sljivancanin may have issued that order. Would you agree that it was possible that Sljivancanin issued that order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I disagree, and I have told you so already.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, let's continue. You testified that while at the hospital, you met Marin Vidic and you transported him to the security organ desk at Negoslavci. And that's at pages 27 and 28 of your testimony yesterday. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you took this action in response to an order; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. It wasn't on my own initiative that I took him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And would you agree, sir, that it was Major Sljivancanin who issued that task or order for you to transport Marin Vidic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The fact that you don't remember, are you saying that it was possible, then, that he issued that order?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't want to speculate now. I told you that I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, let's see if we can refresh your recollection. Let's turn to your 1999 statement to the military court, 0218-8231 to 0218-8234. Page 3 in the English; and B/C/S, 8233. Do you see where it says, "I remember that day around 0900 hours per security organ's order," in the middle? Do you see that, "I remember that day around 0900 hours per security organ's order."

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: It says, "I remember that day, around 0900 hours, per security organ's order gave a ride to Marin Vidic Republic of Croatia trustee, who was at the hospital to the brigade command position. I gave him a ride. I left him at the command position, and I returned to the hospital. In the meantime, Vesna Bosanac was brought there." Did I read that correctly?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, you did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said that you gave him a ride pursuant to the security organ's order. The security organ was Major Sljivancanin; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you say about Sljivancanin being the organ, no. Sljivancanin was the chief of security organ, and there were a number of other officers belonging to the security organ. So somebody called via communication channels and conveyed the order to me to take this person, in order to gain some information, collect information, I don't know what it was about. It doesn't say here: Per security -- per order of the chief of security organ, no. It just says per security organ's order, although I wrote here -- I stated in this statement "ordered," yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So someone, you're saying, in the security organ ordered you to bring Vidic to the security organ desk at Negoslavci. That's what you said.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what it says there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you say, "that's what it says," that's what you said in 1999 to the military court.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is true that I stated that, but had I read it in greater detail and understood its importance, I probably would have modified this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And that's all speculation, sir, isn't that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it's not speculation. I'm telling you how it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, are you aware that there has been testimony in this case that Major Sljivancanin ordered or tasked you to transport Marin Vidic to the headquarters; are you aware of that? And that's at page 13595.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that case. But even had it been so, I don't see anything bad, although I see what you're driving at. This person needed to be interviewed by security organs. I don't see anything bad about such an order, even if it was the case; however, I don't remember it being the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, is it true, as that testimony appears, that Major Sljivancanin ordered you to drive Marin Vidic to Negoslavci and that you obeyed the order and did so? Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No one made mention of Major Sljivancanin. I don't remember receiving such an order from him.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, on page 13595 of this trial, Major Sljivancanin has testified that he gave you the task of transporting Mr. Vidic. Are you saying that the accused, Sljivancanin, isn't telling the truth?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not saying decidedly. I'm not 100 percent certain. I'm only saying that I don't recall who transmitted this order to me. It might have been him, because he was in the hospital area. But I see nothing terrible about this because it's the security organ that's dealing with this person. I'm not taking him to the brigade command; I'm taking him to the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And the security organ can issue orders to you, isn't that correct, just like he did for you to transport Marin Vidic?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I repeat again: The security organ cannot issue orders, that is the chief of the security organ. You keep insisting on this one case which, in my view, is not really important.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So when Major Sljivancanin, according to his testimony, ordered or tasked you to bring Marin Vidic to Negoslavci, we should reject that testimony; is that what you're saying?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's up to you to decide. Maybe Major Sljivancanin doesn't remember some things so well. I am not -- I'm not asserting that. He might remember them better than me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You testified yesterday and today that the order was relayed to you by radio, and that was the reason that you don't know who issued that order. Do you recall that testimony? That's on page 59 yesterday.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I said yesterday, to the best of my recollection. That's a detail which is difficult to recall, but I remember with 100 percent certainty that I personally conducted him there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would it surprise you that Major Sljivancanin testified at pages 13593 to 594 that while he was with you at the hospital, he gave you that task? So you didn't receive any notice by radio.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's his statement. He may have better recollection, or I may have a better recollection.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So based on Major Sljivancanin's recollection and testimony, would you agree that he issued you orders and tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would not agree.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So when he's testified to having issued you orders and tasks, it's just a figment of his imagination?

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Weiner --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I will withdraw that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Are you in the middle of that issue or --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I'm waiting before turning to that objection to see whether you have finished that point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good. Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BULATOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I think Mr. Sljivancanin, in his testimony, nowhere said what Mr. Weiner is trying to put to the witness as Mr. Sljivancanin's testimony, that he issued him tasks in the plural, to give the impression that Sljivancanin was constantly giving tasks. But we are now talking about one single task, the taking away of Marin Vidic. So I believe counsel is misleading the witness by using the plural, "tasks" allegedly given by Sljivancanin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you finished with the point, Mr. Weiner?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I will withdraw the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You withdraw it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like to discuss a few other areas of your testimony today and yesterday. And you testified that you knew or you were aware that the buses would be going to the barracks; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I knew, that they were going to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you were questioned previously in 1995 -- I'm sorry, 1999, and 2005 in Belgrade, you indicated that you were not aware of where the buses were going; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: One might say it's correct because, of course, they wouldn't remain at the barracks. What I meant to say was I didn't know where they would go on from the barracks. That's probably the gist of what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, that's not the gist of what you said. Let us go to the testimony. Let's start out with your statement of 1999, which is 0218-8231, 0218-8234, page 3 in the English. Can you move down a little bit, please. Thank you. Do you see the next to last paragraph, sir? "After that, I think it was on the 20th of November, 1991." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: "After that, I think it was on the 20th of November, 1991, evacuation started of people who were in the hospital. Previously, some sort of selection was done. Selection was done by security organs, so some people were separated to go to Croatia, some to go to Vojvodina, and some were held and moved into the buses that transported them somewhere, but I do not know where." "I only know that my unit got a task to secure one group of civilians that were separated. They were supposed to go to Croatia, but the Croatian side did not want to take them over and they had to return. They were transported again and I know that they were turned over to Croatians, but I do not know where." Now, you never said that these people had been transported to the barracks, did you?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. With respect to this question, I was responding to a question by Mr. Domazet, because the evacuation of civilians was carried out later from the hospital. And it was those buses I was referring to when I said that I didn't know where they would go. I knew that some people wanted to go to Croatia; and later on, I learned that there had been some problems about their being received there. That's what I was referring to in this passage. I think my reply to Mr. Domazet was similar to the reply I gave you concerning this question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you never mentioned the word "barracks" in this statement, isn't that correct, in relation to the buses leaving the hospital?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, you were asked again in Belgrade about -- at the special court in 2005 about this situation. And if we go to page 12 in the English, which is 0461-9343 to 0461-9395; page 12, 0461-9350. Pages 12, which is 9350, going into page 13. It would be 9350. Now, do you see where the presiding judge says "yes," it's in the middle: "Yes, you say here that everyone was evacuated from the hospital on November 20th." Do you see that? Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The presiding judge: "Yes, you say here that everyone was evacuated from the hospital on 20 November. But earlier, a selection or separation was carried out by security organs; and some were singled out to go to Croatia, some to Vojvodina, and some were kept back and put in buses which took them somewhere but I don't know where." "Witness Radoje Paunovic: That's right. I don't know where they were driven to. I just know, based on the statements of some regulars who were doing their military service and who accompanied them to the barracks. I don't know whether there were one or two buses, that's where their assignment ended. And as I said, there was a selection because I was present, not that I took part, but I saw people there; for instance, one would say he wanted to go to Croatia, another towards Serbia or Vojvodina, and that's what I meant in that context." "Could one conclude that there was a third group that wasn't going to either Croatia or to Vojvodina but to some buses which drove away, but you don't know where? "I don't know but I assume -- no, I don't assume. They were driven to the barracks. I know that some were driven to the barracks, whether it was one or two. I don't know, because I did not personally issue any assignments to that military patrol, nor did I participate in the selection. I mean, neither I nor members of my unit did, other personnel did." Sir, you never said that you knew, prior to those buses leaving, that they'd be going to the barracks. You learned that from people who had gone to the barracks; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What you are reading here, my statement, where it says who is going to Croatia, who is going to Vojvodina, those are completely different people. Those are civilians. This is correct, that a certain number of soldiers went to the barracks. But I said, both yesterday and today, that I am not aware that they went in the direction of Ovcara or any other facility. We are mixing things up here. So let me emphasise once again. It was not only those suspect or suspected members of Croatian paramilitary formations that were in the hospital; there were also civilians there and members of the general population. So when they were evacuated, they expressed their wishes as to where they wanted to go. That's why I said I don't know to what destinations these buses went. These what I meant to say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, you never said that you knew, prior to those buses leaving, that they were heading to the barracks. You found out after they went to the barracks from the -- your soldiers, your police officers who escorted them there; isn't that correct? Yes or no.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't recall, so I can't give you a yes or no answer. But I'm sure that I received reports through their commanders from some soldiers that they went to the barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you agree, sir, that you may have learned after the fact that they had gone to the barracks?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the case of some of the buses, not all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Thank you. You testified today that a -- you saw a Colonel Pavkovic at the hospital. You didn't say that he was in charge of the evacuation, but you said you thought then maybe he was in charge of the evacuation. Is that the gist of your testimony, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Prior to testifying in this court, had you ever said to anyone -- have you ever stated in any court or in any statement that Colonel Pavkovic was in charge of the evacuation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, I never said anything like that. I am not sure even today that he was in charge of the evacuation. It's only my opinion that he might have been. Whether he actually was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You spoke with the Office of the Prosecutor in July of 2005, and if we go to that statement, on page 61 -- I'm sorry, paragraph 61, page 12, 0423-8944, and paragraph 61 is on 0423-8955. You stated in paragraph 61: "I never saw a written order for the evacuation of the Vukovar Hospital. I assume that there was a written order taking into account the complexity of such an operation. I do not remember who informed me or how I was informed. I did not know either who was to be in charge of the evacuation." You never knew who was in charge of the evacuation.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And when you said today that Colonel Pavkovic was in charge of the evacuation, you said that to help your friend Major Sljivancanin; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that's the way I put it. If I stated that, then when I was talking about Pavkovic, he might have been, because I saw him around at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you --

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But that has nothing to do whether Sljivancanin is a friend of mine or not. I am testifying here as a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: In fact, in your statement at paragraph 67, your statement to the OTP, you indicated that it was possible that Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I may have stated something to that effect, but I certainly never stated anywhere that Sljivancanin was in charge. I may have said in that statement -- may I comment on paragraph 67, what you're asking me about?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Please do.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This reply in paragraph 67, the court investigator put a document to me or maybe put something to me orally saying that Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation. And right at the start of this paragraph, my reply is, I quote: "At that time, I did not know that Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Would you like to continue reading, sir.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. "It is up to the security organs to first interview the persons who are to be evacuated and to select them. The military police then has to carry -- or has to conduct the evacuees and hand them over to the authorities as agreed. It is most logical for the commander of the military police unit to be in command of the transport and hand-over." "In the case of Vukovar Hospital, it is not clear whether the evacuees were prisoners of war. So it does not seem illogical to me that the security organ was in charge of the operation, because they were the ones carrying out the selection. I do admit that the selection process is only one of the aspects of evacuation."

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: When you said: "It does not seem illogical to me to appoint the security organ as the one in charge of the operation, because they carried out the selection," you're indicating that Major Sljivancanin could have been in charge of that evacuation operation; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not correct, sir. I said that the investigator put to me - I don't know on what basis - that it was Major Sljivancanin who was in charge of the operation. So my reply followed from that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you said: "It does not seem illogical to me to appoint a security organ as the one in charge of the operation, because they carried out the selection." Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. Please don't put your ideas into my statement. I didn't say that he was in charge. But that based on evidence put to me, I don't remember what. Even if he had been, I didn't think about this but that's not how I saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But you said: "It wouldn't seem illogical to appoint a security organ as the one in charge of the operation, because they carried out the selection." Those are your words, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't see anything bad in what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, you know that the person who Colonel Mrksic placed in charge of an evacuation operation has certain powers and duties, and can issue orders to others, isn't that correct, to facilitate that operation?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about that yesterday and today. I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You know, having been a soldier for your career, that a person who is placed in charge by a commander of a military operation has the powers and authority to issue orders to those persons and units participating in that operation; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are working on the basis of a hypothetical case, and you are quoting our rules. I don't see anything contentious there, but you keep focussing on one person only.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Well, sir, if Major Sljivancanin was in charge of that evacuation operation, he had the authority to issue orders to you and your -- and the members of your military police unit; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't answer that question because the same questions -- or rather, similar questions were put by an investigator, and I gave answers of this nature, which now you are interpreting to your advantage or as it suits you best.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, there's a question: If Major Sljivancanin was in charge of that evacuation operation, he had the authority to issue orders to you and the members of your military police unit; isn't that correct? Can you answer that.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And if Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation operation, he had the authority to say to you: "Take Marin Vidic from the hospital and drive him to Negoslavci." And you would obey his order; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, you are phrasing it in terms of a hypothesis. Ask me about specific cases. I don't want to work on the basis of assumptions here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Sir, there has been testimony that Marin Vidic was driven from the hospital to Negoslavci as a result of orders given. That was your testimony. If Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation operation, he had authority to issue those orders to you, and you had to obey him. And that's what happened; isn't that correct, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once again, it isn't correct. When I took Marin Vidic, the evacuation of the hospital was completed. And one cannot link Marin Vidic with the evacuation of the hospital at all, or rather, I apologise, I first took Marin Vidic and then the evacuation was carried out. I'm sorry, that was -- I'm sorry, that was the slip of the tongue.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So why don't you try my question. If Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the evacuation operation, isn't it true that he would have the authority to issue the orders to you to take Marin Vidic to Negoslavci, and you would have to obey him. And that's exactly what happened.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why are you always bringing up Sljivancanin? Why don't you bring up another name in charge of the operation? I don't understand this question. You are asking me to speculate.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: You're here to testify. You've been called to testify on behalf of the accused, Major Sljivancanin. And that's why I'm asking you questions about him and the other accused. And you still haven't answered my question. Would you like me to repeat it again?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't need to repeat it. You want me to say that Major Sljivancanin was in charge of the operation. I keep insisting on the fact that I don't know that he was in charge of the operation, and I am not aware of any orders.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But the question was, sir: If he was in charge of the operation, he had the right and authority to order you to bring Mr. Vidic to Negoslavci, and you had to obey that order, and that's what happened; isn't that correct? You can say yes, you can say no, or refuse to answer.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say either yes or no, and I'm not refusing to answer. Let me repeat, I took Marin Vidic on the 19th in the evening, and the operation of the hospital evacuation began on the 20th, and I don't see any link there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: While we're on the 19th, let's move briefly to another subject. You testified today in response to counsel for the accused Radic that it was not possible for people to have entered the hospital while it was under the control of your military police unit. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Now, sir, on the 19th and the 24th of November, you weren't present at that hospital on a 24-hour basis; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And you can only answer or provide information about those times that you were present at the hospital; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Concerning certain information, yes, and other information, no, because the company commander informed me about the events which took place in my absence, that is to say, Captain First Class Simic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But again, you can't state whether or not people entered that hospital while you were not present; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can state, because I believe my company commander. He was the one informing me, as I told you, that nobody came in or out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: But if you weren't there, sir, you can't state whether or not people entered or left the hospital.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I told you what my position was and why.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: May the witness be shown his testimony from Belgrade, page 44 and 45 of the Belgrade transcript. On the e-tran system, it's 0461-9343 to 0461-9395; page 0461-9365 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: Could you go to the middle of the page, sir. "Presiding Judge: Despite the security, do you know whether any residents of Vukovar entered the hospital to visit?" Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a minute, please. Would you please give me the beginning again, the beginning of the quotation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: The speaker is the Presiding Judge asking a question: "Despite the security, do you know whether any residents of Vukovar entered the hospital to visit?"

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: All right. So question: "Despite the security, do you know whether any of the residents of Vukovar entered the hospital to visit?" "Witness Radoje Paunovic: No one entered the hospital. "Presiding Judge: To their relatives, friends, and so on to perhaps even lead them out. "Natasa Cannedic: That someone came out of the hospital? "Presiding Judge: And perhaps they took someone out. "Witness Radoje Paunovic: No. "Presiding Judge: For instance, Mr. Vujanovic, that Vujanovic whom you know, let out his sister. "Witness Radoje Paunovic: I told you that I wasn't there continuously. I'm talking about what I know while I was there. As to whether Vujanovic or whoever came, if you ask me, I'm telling you that I don't know. I'm not saying that this didn't happen, but I don't know about it." Did I read that correctly, sir?

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: So you can't tell if people entered or exited the hospital while you weren't there, according to your testimony in Belgrade.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My statement is true, and I stand by it. The president of the chamber, as you can see here, didn't put any documents to me. He just said that Mr. Vujanovic had taken out his sister. I don't know about that case. And who knows whether this pertains to the 19th at all, this issue with Vujanovic. As I have stated to you, I wasn't at the hospital the entire time. But based on the reports I received from the company commander, nobody came in or out.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEINER
utterances.text: And as you said: "I'm talking about what I know while I was there. As to whether Vujanovic or whoever came, if you ask me, I'm telling you that I don't know. I'm not saying that this didn't happen, but I don't know about it." And when you said that, sir, you're indicating you only knew what happened while you were there; isn't that correct? That's what you told the court.

utterances.speaker: RADOJE PAUNOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct, that I said this in this statement. I failed to say in this statement that perhaps Vujanovic took somebody out prior to this. But let me repeat, my company commander didn't inform me about such instances. And why would I not testify on the basis of the information I received from the company commander, when previously you asked me to speculate about certain issues. I'm not denying this. I wasn't in the hospital constantly. There's nothing contentious here. I stand by this statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Borovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. BOROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Even though I think that the witness has already explained this, I think we need to say that we are spending too much time on this, because I didn't put this to the witness. What I put to the witness was whether any soldiers or officers went into the hospital to mistreat the wounded, and the answer was clear, nobody. Now, another instance is being put to the witness when the sister was taken out. I think that my learned friend Weiner is belabouring the point without a solid reason.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: He won't be able to belabour it any more, Mr. Borovic, because we've reached the time when we must adjourn for the day. So we adjourn now. We resume tomorrow at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 8th day of November, 2006, at 9.00 a.m. 19 20 21 22 23 24 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 1.47 p.m.,
